questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose this destination mainly because the university offers a certificate in transnational law, which also includes the opportunity to take courses at the Geneva Graduate Institute

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Most things are explained at the welcome session.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It is mainly when you are leaving that you are not really informed about what to do. When you receive a letter about insurance you need to send a picture of you EU health card but this is not explained by Arnuad or the OCPM.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: The university offers housing at cité universitaire and through the BLOG. It can be difficult to get accommodation so I would recommend applying both at cité and also trying to get a room through BLOG.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Cité universitaire is good if you want to socialise a lot and it has a gym, tennis and padel courts and football next to it. The BLOG offers both rooms and studios - these accommodations are generally nicer than cité.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You register for courses after the beginning of classes. Later you have to register for exams.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The course registration was explained at the faculty information session.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was able to register for all the classes I wanted at the university. I was only able to get my second priority at the Graduate Institute.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Apply for many courses at the graduate institute as there is not much space in the courses. Remember to apply for both exams and courses separately - they are very strict about this.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The difficulty of the courses varies a lot. Some are very easy (like international arbitration) and some are quite difficult (like practise of IHL).

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style was mostly lectures. Some classes give a bonus for active participation and some have mandatory active participation (like the ones at the Graduate Institute).

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Comparative Methodology: Contract Law, Comparative human rights, Practise of International Humanitarian law, International Arbitration, Business and Human Rights: Law, Politics, Policy (at the Graduate Institute)

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Comparative Methodology: Contract Law (or tort law) is mandatory if you want the CTL, but it is very interesting (and easy) courses and the teacher is good. International Arbitration is very easy. Practise of International Humanitarian law is very interesting but quite difficult.

Housing DKK per month *

Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Geneva is one of the most expensive cities to live in. I recommend going to France for shopping (its very easy to do).

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The transportation in the Canton of Geneva is free for students under 25 (even if you live in France). You did not have to buy a lot of books for uni - only in contract law.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There very many athletic activities available through the university. Socially it was mainly ESN that had events. The university sometimes had cultural events at Uni Mail such as food stands from many different countries.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would highly recommend going to ESN events (and signing up early because there are usually limited spaces) as you will meet a lot of different people from different countries. The events are not really well planned but they can be very fun.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Not much goes on in Geneva during the weekends so I recommend taking trips to other cities close by like Paris, Zurich, Annecy etc.. There are many good hiking places.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy - Geneva is very international and quite similar to Denmark in many ways

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It is a bit difficult to socialise with local students as Swiss people are a bit reserved

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The city is very quiet especially during the day in the weekend and evenings during the week.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The city is very international.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Geneva is not the most exciting place, but it is good if you want to work with international law. Making friends with people from different countries can make the experience a lot more fun. I recommend going during the spring semester as it is more fun than the fall semester.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Making friends with people from other nationalities

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Saving money

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
